question: In cricket, a full - pitched ball aimed at the batsman’s toes or on the crease line is called ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yorker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A yorker is a delivery in cricket that lands on or near the batsman's toes or the crease line.
 
• It is bowled to target the base of the stumps or the batsman's feet.
 
• Yorkers are typically used to prevent batsmen from scoring runs, especially in the death overs of limited-overs cricket.
 
• They are difficult to hit because they arrive at the batsman very quickly and give them less time to adjust their shot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Googly**

 
 
• A googly is a type of delivery bowled by a leg-spinner. It is designed to deceive the batsman by turning in the opposite direction to a normal leg break.
 
• When bowled by a right-arm leg-spinner, a googly turns from the off side to the leg side for a right-handed batsman.
 
• It is also known as a 'wrong'un'.
 
 
 
• **Zooter**
 
 
• A zooter is a type of delivery bowled by a leg-spinner. It is typically flatter and faster than a normal leg break.
 
• The zooter is often used to deceive the batsman by not spinning or by skidding through low after pitching.
 
 
 
• **Waft**
 
 
• A waft is an informal term used to describe a careless or wild shot played by a batsman.
 
• It generally refers to a shot where the batsman swings the bat without much control or precision.
